title: You start with an all-water grid and add land one cell at a time. After each addition, report the current number of islands. Use Union-Find with path compression and union by size.
shortTitle: Number of Islands II (Dynamic) — running island count as land is added

s1_definition.profdef: Maintain a dynamic Union-Find keyed by flattened cell index. Each land addition first increments the island count by one (a new singleton island), then unions the new cell with each already-land neighbor; every successful union decrements the count. Adding land to an existing land cell is a no-op. Reporting after each operation gives the running counts in O((rows·cols + k)·α) total.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India activates service in map cells one at a time. Each newly activated cell starts as its own region, raising the region count by one. If it touches an already-active neighbor, those regions fuse and the count drops. After each activation you announce how many separate regions currently exist.
s1_definition.oneliner: Each new land cell adds one island, then every merge with a live neighbor subtracts one — report the count after each step.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Maintain a dynamic Union-Find keyed by flattened cell index. Each land addition first increments the island count by one (a new singleton island), then unions the new cell with each already-land neighbor; every successful union decrements the count. Adding land to an existing land cell is a no-op. Reporting after each operation gives the running counts in O((rows·cols + k)·α) total.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** National Bank of India activates service in map cells one at a time. Each newly activated cell starts as its own region, raising the region count by one. If it touches an already-active neighbor, those regions fuse and the count drops. After each activation you announce how many separate regions currently exist.

**One line to remember:** Each new land cell adds one island, then every merge with a live neighbor subtracts one — report the count after each step.

sections.s2_technical:
Keep a boolean "is this cell land" via the parent map and a running count. When a position is added and is already land, do nothing. For example: `if (isLand[idx]) { result.add(count); continue; }`.

Otherwise mark it land, increment the count, and union with each of the four neighbors that is already land, decrementing on each real merge. For example: `count++; for (nb : neighbors) if (isLand[nb] && union(idx, nb)) count--;`.

Record the count after each operation into the result list. The total time is proportional to the grid plus the number of operations, each at near-constant cost, with union by size keeping trees shallow.

A senior nuance is that ordinary Union-Find cannot handle land removal because it has no split operation; supporting removal requires offline processing in reverse (treating removals as additions) or a link-cut structure, which is a common follow-up to probe depth.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, a rollout activates service cells one at a time, and after each activation the operations team needs the current number of contiguous service regions for staffing. This is exactly how dynamic island counting works.

Problem 2 — Activating a cell that is already active must not change anything. This is exactly why a repeated position is a no-op in the running count.

The mini-project builds a `DynamicRegionCounter`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input is a three-by-three grid and four activations.

Step 1: Activating (0,0) creates the first region; count is one.

Step 2: Activating (0,1) is adjacent to (0,0), so after adding one and merging one the count stays at one.

Step 3: Activating (1,2) has no active neighbor, so it is a new region; count becomes two.

Step 4: Activating (2,1) has no active neighbor, so it is a new region; count becomes three.

Step 5: The running counts are one, one, two, three.

```text
2026-10-26T23:30:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — Rollout Dynamic Region Counter
2026-10-26T23:30:00Z [INFO] After activating (0,0) regions=1
2026-10-26T23:30:00Z [INFO] After activating (0,1) regions=1
2026-10-26T23:30:00Z [INFO] After activating (1,2) regions=2
2026-10-26T23:30:00Z [INFO] After activating (2,1) regions=3
2026-10-26T23:30:00Z [INFO] Running counts: [1, 1, 2, 3]
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```text
  add(0,0): +1 island          → 1
  add(0,1): +1, merge w/(0,0)  → 1
  add(1,2): +1, no neighbor    → 2
  add(2,1): +1, no neighbor    → 3
  result = [1,1,2,3]
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Number of Islands II is the dynamic version where land is added one cell at a time and I must report the island count after each addition. I maintain a Union-Find keyed by the flattened cell index together with a running island counter. Each time a new land cell is added, I first increment the counter because that cell is initially its own island, then I try to union it with each of its four neighbors that is already land, decrementing the counter on every union that genuinely merges two separate islands. If the position being added is already land, I treat it as a no-op and just repeat the current count.

Using path compression with union by size keeps the trees shallow, so the whole sequence runs in time proportional to the grid plus the number of operations, each at effectively constant cost.

In my project at National Bank of India, a service rollout activated map cells one at a time and operations needed the current number of contiguous service regions after each activation for staffing. The interviewer's favorite follow-up is land removal, and the honest answer is that plain Union-Find has no split operation, so removal is handled offline by processing the timeline in reverse and treating each removal as an addition, or by a more advanced link-cut structure.
